result.title: Certify, Report, or Refuse: Harm-Constrained Conformal Prediction for Clinical Actions
result.comment: Findings of the 6th Machine Learning for Health Symposium (ML4H 2026)
result.summary: Routing a melanoma case to routine follow-up is a serious action error that diagnostic coverage alone does not rule out. We present Harm-Constrained Risk-Optimal Conformal Prediction (HC-ROCP), a training-free framework that uses frozen classifier probabilities and adds a harm penalty when choosing prediction sets and actions. We test the resulting policies on disjoint calibration splits with multiplicity adjustment. HC-ROCP certifies supported claims, reports descriptive fallback policies, and refuses unsupported subgroup claims. We evaluate these outputs retrospectively on COVID-19 radiographs, ISIC 2019 dermoscopy, and EyePACS-to-APTOS retinopathy transfer. Across ten calibration seeds, HC-ROCP reduces COVID-19 severe-action errors from the exact risk-optimal baseline's 4.68\% to 0.54\%. At a 5\% budget, global claims are certified for COVID-19 and ISIC, but the rare squamous-cell-carcinoma claim is refused. At 1\%, all settings receive descriptive reports. For each budget, we also report the minimum severe-case count needed to pass the global harm gate with zero errors, providing a starting point for further data collection.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 HC-ROCP，一种无需训练的 conformal prediction 框架：在冻结分类器概率基础上加入危害惩罚来选择预测集与临床动作，并以「认证 / 描述性报告 / 拒绝」三种输出处理子群主张；在 COVID-19 胸片、ISIC 2019 皮肤镜与 EyePACS→APTOS 迁移上做回溯评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按风险预算决定「认证、降级报告或拒绝」的三级输出，可能为 LVR 中证据不足时的 STOP／弃答准则与子群风险控制提供概念参照，但与 latent 状态生成无直接关系，需核查其危害门限是否可迁移为推理停止判据。
